findings.text: non-blocking: the after_suite and tests commands both name only tests/test_a_limit_reset_reaches_every_pane.py and tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py, so neither arm runs tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py, the file the gained commit 802af47998 adds its case to and the file whose assertions this node rewrote; the only evidence the final commit's case is green and load-bearing is the targeted negative control logs/negative-control-job-column.log (1 failed, 7 deselected, EXIT=1) and a single-test read at the head.

non-blocking: the landing record names 8575a8ebc as the measured head and at line 60 states the write-scope grant is still unrecorded, while the reviewed head is 802af479986f, node.write_paths in the run's live pointer now carries tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py, and the fragment says nothing about the final commit's job-column case or its negative control.

non-blocking: the fragment cites logs/negative-control-scope-prewiden.log as holding the read-only OSError from the widen attempt, but that log is the manifest audit output (command: reckon crew check --manifest) and the OSError is in logs/scope-widen-refused.log, so a reader following the pointer finds the wrong evidence.

non-blocking: assert rendered.split()[1] == ticker.LIMIT_STAGE compares the rendered stage cell against the renderer's own constant, so a change to that constant moves both sides together and the done_when's 'stage cell reads limit' is not pinned to a literal anywhere; the same shape stands at line 388 and at line 170 of the pre-existing case.

non-blocking: the done_when requires tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py to pass at head and both arms record it failing with the same id (reported honestly under outside_scope), and the head arm logs/repair2-after.log runs serially in the worker worktree where the done_when asks both arms to come from git checkouts under the run scratch with pytest -n 8.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit from b665d7481695 to 802af479986f; the single gained commit is test-only and adds one case to tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py:234-248 comparing the column where limits reset starts for two differently named groups, which I ran at the head and found green.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks for a follower-driven case whose stage cell reads limit and whose line carries limits reset, continue and worker lanes keep their limits with no transition; tests/test_a_limit_reset_reaches_every_pane.py:187-209 is that case and logs/repair2-after.log records it passing, but the same done_when requires tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py to pass at head and both arms fail it.
item_verdicts.goal: the source node's goal is that a reset row tells orchestrator sessions to continue and opens no worker lane; at the reviewed head reckon/crew/ticker.py:3151-3193 composes the row as stage limit, group in the job cell and the clause from limit_reset_text, and the gained commit touches no production code.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the repair arms at 1 failed 17 passed either side of b665d748 with the same failure id, the 24-file ticker/lift_watch sweep at 159 against 160 passed, the transition-restoration control at 3 failed 11 passed EXIT=1, the job-column control at 1 failed 7 deselected EXIT=1, and names every log.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the run's recorded write paths in the live pointer: they carry all seven paths the landed diff touches, including tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py, so the prior round's blocking scope finding is answered; the gained commit's only path, that same test file, is inside the scope.

justifications.durability: tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py:244 fails when the job cell is sized by its own text, shown by logs/negative-control-job-column.log at 1 failed, but the stage word is asserted against ticker.LIMIT_STAGE at tests/test_a_limit_reset_reaches_every_pane.py:204 so a change to that constant would move both sides.
justifications.evidence: logs/repair2-after.log is a real arm at 802af47998 ending EXIT=1 with one pre-existing failure, but it never runs tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py, the done_when's required module-window pass is unmet at both arms, and the manifest records no ruff log for a done_when clause I had to measure myself (delta zero on all four changed files).
justifications.fit: tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py:234-248 follows the module's producer-path fixture idiom and its docstring, and the production code mirrors _lift_line at reckon/crew/ticker.py:3196-3230 rather than inventing a row shape.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/ticker.py:3176-3193 draws stage limit, the padded job cell and the clause from limit_reset_text, so a claude-orchestrators reset prints 'limits reset (five_hour): orchestrator sessions continue; worker lanes keep their limits' and a claude-sub reset closes with the worker-lane clause alone.
justifications.reuse: the gained commit adds one test and no definition; the production change routes the row through the existing _job_name and _job_cell at reckon/crew/ticker.py:2776 and :2942 and composes the wording once in limit_reset_text at :371, and no other reset-clause or job-cell owner exists under reckon/crew.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff is inside the run's recorded write paths, which now carry tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py, and the gained commit touches only that file plus nothing outside the plan's fragment clause.
